## The Fork

You are already on a trajectory. The [destructive economy](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] is {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP right now. If current relative growth rates continue, it reaches {{< var destructive_economy_pct_gdp_year_15 >}} by year 15, the failed-state danger zone in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_25pct_gdp >}}, and parity with the productive economy in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}}.

That is the baseline you are comparing everything against. Not a neutral world. Not a stable world. A world where extraction, cybercrime, and militarized waste keep compounding while the productive economy tries to outrun them.

The [Minimum Sustainable Trajectory (1% Treaty)](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] projects {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_multiplier >}} lifetime income and {{< var treaty_hale_gain_year_15 >}} additional healthy years by year 15. The [Wishonian](../futures/wishonia.qmd) [Optimal Governance Trajectory](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) projects {{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_multiplier >}} and {{< var wishonia_hale_gain_year_15 >}}. PRIZE deposits are not mainly about earning on the deposit itself. They are about nudging civilization toward the branch where the rest of your life is vastly richer, healthier, and less collapse-prone.

## The Four Futures

| Future | What the model gives you |
|---|---|
| **Failed-State Trajectory** | Roughly {{< var current_trajectory_cumulative_lifetime_income >}} in cumulative lifetime income for the average person, with destructive activity rising from {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP now toward {{< var destructive_economy_pct_gdp_year_15 >}} by year 15. |
| **Minimum Sustainable Trajectory ([1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd))** | {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} in additional lifetime income, {{< var treaty_hale_gain_year_15 >}} additional healthy years by year 15, and {{< var treaty_personal_upside_blend >}} in blended upside. |
| **[Wishonian](../futures/wishonia.qmd) [Optimal Governance Trajectory](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd)** | {{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} in additional lifetime income, {{< var wishonia_hale_gain_year_15 >}} additional healthy years by year 15, and {{< var wishonia_personal_upside_blend >}} in blended upside. |
| **Collapse Tail** | {{< var moronia_trajectory_probability_year_20 >}} probability in the repo's year-20 EV framing, with the destructive economy reaching 25% of GDP in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_25pct_gdp >}} and 50% in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}} if the loop is not broken. |

The paper exists because that spread is absurdly large and most humans still treat "do nothing" as if it were safe.

## How It Works (The 90-Second Version)

**PRIZE deposits** fund the prize pool. You deposit funds into the same pool that compounds through the wishocratic fund model until year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}. If, at that point, global HALE has not reached {{< var wishonia_projected_hale_year_15 >}} and global median income has not reached {{< var wishonia_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}}, depositors divide the realized pool pro rata by deposits. If both targets are met, the same realized pool distributes to VOTE claimants. PRIZE is catalytic committed capital, not a redeem-anytime savings account. It stays with the depositor's verified account or legal-entity account until resolution, subject to recovery and lawful successor control. It only routes to VOTE claimants on verified success. See the [prize protocol](../appendix/earth-optimization-prize-protocol.qmd) [@earth-optimization-prize-protocol-paper-2025] for the full specification.

| Metric | Current baseline | Year 15 target | Source |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| **Global HALE** | {{< var global_hale_current >}} | {{< var wishonia_projected_hale_year_15 >}} | Closing the entire {{< var global_hale_gap >}} health-adjusted life expectancy gap |
| **Global median income** | {{< var current_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} (status quo at year 15) | {{< var wishonia_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}} | {{< var wishonia_trajectory_gdp_vs_current_trajectory_multiplier_year_15 >}} the status quo trajectory |

**VOTE claims** are the allocation mechanism. Recruit a verified referendum participant, earn one. On success, VOTE holdings determine your share of the PRIZE pool. VOTE stays with the verified account that earned it. It is not publicly tradable inside the protocol, so recruitment credit stays with recruiters rather than speculators. Registration asks two questions: (1) yes or no on the [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] ("Should 1% of military spending be redirected to clinical trials?"), and (2) how much military vs. clinical trials, with Optimitron [@optimocracy-paper-2025] evidence (cost per DALY, lives saved per dollar, economic returns per dollar). 30 seconds. Optional deeper [wishocratic](../solution/wishocracy.qmd) allocation available afterward.

**Why these claims are not publicly tradable.** Tradability would buy liquidity and price discovery. It would also invert the PRIZE signal, weaken early recruitment incentives, and let outsiders buy coalition credit without doing coalition work. The public signal this design relies on is simpler: verified participant count, referendum growth, and a visible pool of committed capital. Polls are ignorable. Petitions are ignorable. {{< var treaty_campaign_voting_bloc_target_nounit >}} verified participants and a large committed prize pool are harder to dismiss.

The obvious Goodhart objection: median metrics can be gamed. If the sickest die faster, median health rises. But mortality is binary and hard to fake across millions of people. Median income requires improving the middle of the distribution, not just the top. And the adversarial challenge window means anyone who catches gaming can post a bond, present evidence, and claw back the payout.

## Why A Rational Person Should Care

The arithmetic is the point. For the average human on Earth today, the model already implies {{< var global_avg_income_2025 >}} annual income, {{< var global_avg_remaining_years >}} remaining life, and roughly {{< var global_annual_savings_per_capita >}} in annual savings capacity. If you want your own numbers, use the [personal benefits calculator](../call-to-action/your-personal-benefits.qmd).

| Personal upside layer | Treaty | Wishonia |
|---|---|---|
| **Income upside** | {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} | {{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} |
| **Healthy-life upside** | {{< var treaty_hale_value_per_capita >}} | {{< var wishonia_hale_value_per_capita >}} |
| **Blended upside** | {{< var treaty_personal_upside_blend >}} | {{< var wishonia_personal_upside_blend >}} |
| **EV of shifting success by 1 percentage point (income only)** | {{< var contribution_ev_per_pct_point_treaty >}} | {{< var contribution_ev_per_pct_point_wishonia >}} |
| **EV of shifting success by 1 percentage point (blended)** | {{< var contribution_ev_per_pct_point_treaty_blend >}} | {{< var contribution_ev_per_pct_point_wishonia_blend >}} |

Those are not projections about charity. They are projections about your own health, income, and exposure to civilizational failure.

**PRIZE deposits** create visible committed capital. **VOTE claims** reward the coalition-building work of recruitment. The selfish case for the prize is bigger than either instrument. It is the size of the future they are trying to buy.

Everything else in this paper (protocol mechanics, pool growth assumptions, the scoreboard, the numbers) is implementation detail. The [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd) defines the starting benchmark and the rules for replacing it. Before any of it matters, five problems have to be solved. The prize solves all five with one instrument.

## Five Problems, One Instrument

### 1. Nobody Knows Solutions Exist

Most humans have never heard that pragmatic clinical trials cost {{< var dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient >}} per patient (vs. {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}} traditional) [@dfda-impact-paper-2025]. That redirecting 1% of military spending to medical research returns {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025]. That {{< var existing_drugs_efficacy_lag_deaths_total_nounit >}} people have already died waiting for drugs that were proven to work but stuck in regulatory queues [@invisible-graveyard-paper-2025]. That the total cost of buying passage of any policy through legal democratic channels in the United States is {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}}, with ROI exceeding {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} [@cost-of-change-paper-2025].

The prize creates VOTE claims: recruit a verified participant into the [Global Referendum](https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/global-referendum.html), earn a claim on any eventual pool payout. That is enough to make millions of people willing to have a conversation they would otherwise avoid. Each recruitment forces the recruit through evidence (cost per life saved for military spending vs. clinical trials, the efficacy lag death toll, the economic returns). The registration process is the education. The recruitment reward is what makes the education propagate.

### 2. Everyone Who Knows Assumes They Are Alone

Your economists call it pluralistic ignorance. Nearly every human would prefer a world without war and treatable disease, and an extra {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} in lifetime income [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025]. If every human realized that nearly every other human wants the same thing, it would be done tomorrow and the world would be unrecognizable. Instead, everyone assumes massive reform is crazy because they assume nobody else would agree to it. This is the dumbest reason a civilization has ever continued dying.

Every verified registration is a publicly verifiable signal. The scoreboard aggregates across all participating pools in real time. As the number climbs from thousands to millions to hundreds of millions, the belief that "nobody would ever agree to this" becomes empirically falsifiable. You can see that they already did. The [referendum](https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/global-referendum.html) does not create demand for not dying. The demand is there. The scoreboard makes it impossible to pretend it is not.

### 3. The Public Cannot Coordinate Against Concentrated Interests

One of your economists noticed this in 1965 and named it "the logic of collective action" [-@olson1965]. Concentrated interests (defense contractors, pharmaceutical monopolies) face high per-capita stakes and coordinate easily. The general public (dying of untreated diseases, bearing regulatory delay, subsidizing military spending that returns {{< var economic_multiplier_military_spending >}} per dollar [@military-spending-economic-multiplier]) has tiny individual stakes in any single policy fight and cannot mount a proportional response. Your species identified the exact mechanism by which your governance fails, published it, assigned it in universities, and then continued to be governed by it for sixty years.

But Olson's problem is downstream of problems 1 and 2. The public has the money (global household wealth: {{< var global_household_wealth_usd >}}, vs. {{< var concentrated_interest_sector_market_cap_usd >}} held by concentrated opposition sectors [@iab-paper-2025]). It does not have awareness or the coordination mechanism. Once the recruitment incentive has solved the awareness problem and the scoreboard has shattered pluralistic ignorance, PRIZE deposits provide the coordination mechanism: a growing pool of committed money, visible to everyone, that only routes away from depositors when outcomes improve. No central organizer. No charity. No altruism required. Just millions of people acting in financial self-interest, pointed at the same two numbers.

### 4. Nobody Knows Which Solutions to Implement

The prize does not prescribe a solution. It pays for outcomes: median healthy life years and median real after-tax income. Anyone, anywhere, using any legal method, who causes either number to rise gets paid proportionally. The [Earth Optimization Protocol v1](https://manual.warondisease.org) is the terrible starting benchmark, not the answer. It exists because competitions need a starting entry. The prize exists to discover and fund whatever beats it (the Earth Optimization Protocol v2). There are {{< var global_population_2024_nounit >}} of you and AIs that are almost certainly smarter than its authors. If a better design exists, the prize will find it.

This makes the search decentralized. No committee decides which reforms to fund. Millions of financially motivated participants search for, advocate, and implement whatever moves the two numbers. A researcher who discovers a cheaper trial design profits. A lobbyist who passes legislation profits. A nonprofit that recruits a million referendum voters profits. The mechanism is agnostic about how. It engineers the incentives so that the collective intelligence of your entire species is pointed at two measurements instead of scattered across a thousand arguments about which measurement matters.

Your species has tried the obvious alternatives. Advance Market Commitments [@kremer2020] say "we will buy the thing if you build it," which works when the thing is a vaccine but not when the thing is systemic reform. Challenge prizes (the XPRIZE model) give a fixed payout to the first team across the finish line, then stop paying. Direct government procurement funds whatever the procurer thinks will work, which IS the current system, and it IS producing Olsonian capture. Prediction markets tell you what will win but do not cause implementation. Capital-weighted governance systems suffer the same capture problem: the actors with the deepest pockets set the agenda. A prize with published scoring, adversarial challenges, and automatic replacement is the one structure where capturing it requires beating every challenger on verified metrics simultaneously. That is not capture-proof. But it is capture-expensive, which on your planet is the least bad available.

### 5. Complex Reforms Have No On-Ramp

The [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025], FDA reform, wishocratic allocation, cross-jurisdictional policy optimization; each is a hard sell individually. Each requires explaining an elaborate mechanism to people who have been trained to assume nothing works. The prize is the simple entry point. Deposit $1, keep a failure-branch claim on the same pool if nothing works, and help route it to VOTE claimants if the world actually improves. One sentence. One decision. The $1 minimum is the on-ramp, not a claim that every participant must become a large 15-year capital provider.

Once someone makes a PRIZE deposit or earns a VOTE claim, they discover the component reforms through the recruitment and registration process. The treaty. The trial cost data. The allocation evidence. The prize is the funnel into everything else. It converts "this sounds too complicated" into "I put in $1 and either diseases get cured or I still have a claim on the pool, so why not." The complex reforms ride behind the simple instrument.

### The Shared Scoreboard

Problems one through five are structural: awareness, coordination, on-ramps, solution discovery, pluralistic ignorance. But there is a sixth problem underneath all of them. Your species has never built a system that measures the two things everyone agrees on (not dying, earning more), publishes the score, and pays whoever moves it. You argue about drug policy without tracking whether fewer people die. You argue about military spending without tracking whether it makes you safer. You argue about healthcare without tracking whether anyone gets healthier.

The prize does not resolve these arguments. It makes them irrelevant. Two numbers. Did they move? Pay whoever moved them. Every policy debate on Earth becomes "did it raise median healthy life years or median income?" and if the answer is "we don't know," the answer is "then it didn't earn any prize money." For the first time, your species would be focused on tracking shared goals instead of arguing about solutions without measuring whether they work.

## The Exponential Math

On Wishonia, if one person tells two people and each of them tells two people, the math handles the rest. The point is not that everyone becomes a recruiter. The point is that small repeated actions can compound into politically legible scale much faster than most readers intuit.

| Round | Cumulative people | What that looks like |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 0 | 1 | You |
| 10 | 1,024 | A large lecture hall |
| 15 | 32,768 | A small town |
| 20 | 1,048,576 | A city |
| 25 | 33,554,432 | A country |
| 28 | 268,435,456 | Chenoweth passage threshold ({{< var treaty_campaign_voting_bloc_target >}}) |
| 33 | 8,589,934,592 | Everyone on Earth |

28 rounds. Not 28 years. 28 rounds. If each round takes a week, that is seven months. If each round takes a month, that is two years and four months. The important point is not the payout headline. It is that the scoreboard can move from one person to Chenoweth-scale visibility on ordinary human timescales rather than civilizational ones.

The Chenoweth threshold [@3-5-rule] ({{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}} of the population in sustained nonviolent action) has been verified across 323 campaigns since 1900. At {{< var vote_participation_rate >}} expected participation, {{< var vote_expected_participants >}} people vote over the accumulation period, exceeding the Chenoweth threshold by roughly 8x. VOTE claims make coalition-building worth doing. The scoreboard makes that coalition legible. At scale, treaty passage is expected well before the pool matures.

## What A Small Probability Shift Is Worth

Once you understand the mechanism, the next question is what a small increase in success probability is worth to you personally. If the treaty trajectory is even roughly correct, success raises average lifetime income by {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} per person and adds {{< var treaty_hale_value_per_capita >}} in valued healthy-life gains [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025]. Any action you take that shifts implementation probability by even a tiny amount is worth real money to you personally:

| Increase in implementation probability | Treaty income-only EV | Treaty blended EV | Wishonia income-only EV | Wishonia blended EV |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.01 percentage points` | `+$1.49K` | `+$2.48K` | `+$5.21K` | `+$7.56K` |
| `0.1 percentage points` | `+$14.9K` | `+$24.8K` | `+$52.1K` | `+$75.6K` |
| `1 percentage point` | {{< var contribution_ev_per_pct_point_treaty >}} | {{< var contribution_ev_per_pct_point_treaty_blend >}} | {{< var contribution_ev_per_pct_point_wishonia >}} | {{< var contribution_ev_per_pct_point_wishonia_blend >}} |

Those are not projections about other people's welfare. They are projections about your own income, health, and exposure to collapse.

| Channel | What it is | Current modeled range |
|---|---|---|
| You get richer | Per-capita income gain from better resource allocation | {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} (Treaty) to {{< var wishonia_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} (Wishonia) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] |
| You get healthier | Value of additional healthy years by year 15 | {{< var treaty_hale_value_per_capita >}} (Treaty) to {{< var wishonia_hale_value_per_capita >}} (Wishonia) |
| Auxiliary direct upside | VOTE claim payout for verified recruitment | {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}} modeled VOTE payout |
| You lose less | Less exposure to compounding dysfunction tax and collapse | {{< var political_dysfunction_tax_per_person_annual >}}/year ongoing; {{< var moronia_trajectory_probability_year_20 >}} collapse-tail probability at year 20 |
| People stop dying | Lives saved and suffering prevented per probability point you shift | {{< var contribution_dalys_per_pct_point >}} DALYs / {{< var contribution_lives_saved_per_pct_point_nounit >}} lives / {{< var contribution_suffering_hours_per_pct_point >}} suffering hours per percentage point |

**The cost of not acting is not zero.** Political dysfunction already costs {{< var political_dysfunction_tax_per_person_annual >}} per person per year. The [destructive economy](../economics/gdp-trajectories.qmd) [@gdp-trajectories-paper-2025] is already {{< var global_destructive_economy_pct_gdp >}} of GDP, reaches {{< var destructive_economy_pct_gdp_year_15 >}} by year 15, and hits 50% in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}} if current rates continue. "Do nothing" is not a neutral baseline. It is a bet that these trends reverse without intervention.

## This Is a Favorable Bet, Not a Donation

**PRIZE deposits** are the conditional commitment: the same pool compounds until resolution, routes to VOTE claimants on verified success, and stays with depositors pro rata on failure. Your money only leaves the depositor side if someone earned it.

| | If the plan succeeds | If the plan fails |
|---|---|---|
| **A PRIZE deposit** | Pool distributes to VOTE claimants who built the coalition. Your lifetime income rose by {{< var treaty_trajectory_lifetime_income_gain_per_capita >}} like everyone else's. | Depositors divide the realized pool pro rata at year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}. |
| **The world** | Diseases get cured, incomes rise, destructive economy stops compounding | Destructive economy hits 50% of GDP in {{< var destructive_economy_years_to_50pct_gdp >}}; {{< var moronia_trajectory_probability_year_20 >}} probability of collapse trajectory at year 20 |

Mechanisms that keep the same pool intact on failure while only routing it to VOTE claimants on verified success are unusually favorable compared with ordinary political donations.

At the current modeled pool growth rate, the same pool compounds at {{< var prize_pool_annual_return >}} to {{< var prize_pool_15yr_multiple >}} over {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}} years before branch routing. That is a modeling reference, not a guaranteed depositor payout.
:::

The break-even probability shift for any given contribution is small because the per-capita stakes are large:

| Your unreimbursed contribution | Break-even probability shift (Treaty floor) | Break-even probability shift (Wishonia) |
|---|---|---|
| `$1K` | `0.0067%` | `0.0019%` |
| `$10K` | `0.067%` | `0.019%` |
| `$100K` | `0.671%` | `0.192%` |
| `$1M` | `6.71%` | `1.92%` |

But does a $1K contribution actually shift probability by 0.0067%? You do not need to be the marginal dollar that tips the scale. You need to believe that more campaign capital makes success more likely than less, which is nearly tautological for political adoption. Those thresholds also treat PRIZE deposits like unreimbursed spending, so they are biased against contributing. They survive heavy skepticism: if you think the per-capita gain is 100x smaller than modeled, the break-even for $1K is still only 0.67%. The math does not require trusting the model. It requires believing the model is not off by more than four orders of magnitude. And the ceiling cost of achieving the policy change is already bounded: {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} for the United States, {{< var global_political_reform_investment >}} globally, with ROI exceeding {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} for military-to-health reallocation [@cost-of-change-paper-2025].

Outcome-contingent funding and threshold-triggered coordination are standard mechanism-design tools [@tabarrok1998]. The Chenoweth threshold ({{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}}) has been verified across 323 campaigns since 1900. The RECOVERY trial was run by Oxford and published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Every building block is peer-reviewed. The combination is new.

**The free-rider problem has a structural answer.** If success benefits everyone, why not wait and let others pay? Because non-contributors do not earn VOTE claims. They get the population-wide income gain (everyone does), but they miss the VOTE claim payout that recruiters earn. Free-riding means giving up the recruitment reward to save the smallest possible entry ticket. Early contributors raise the probability of success, which raises the expected value for later contributors, creating a coordination game that runs on arithmetic rather than altruism.

Delay is not neutral. Each person can only be recruited once, and every month spent waiting gives the status quo more time to compound while the scoreboard stays smaller than it could be.

## Choose Your Role This Week

| If you are... | In the next 7 days, do this | Visible output |
|---|---|---|
| **A normal participant** | Make a PRIZE deposit, answer the referendum questions, and recruit two verified participants. | One deposit, one completed registration, and two confirmed referrals on the scoreboard. |
| **A builder / critic** | Publish one concrete artifact: a v2 fork, a red-team memo, a metric-gaming attack, or a better implementation-financing design. | A public repo, memo, issue, or brief that other participants can evaluate immediately. |
| **A funder** | Choose one lane and commit real support: seed PRIZE deposits, sponsor referendum infrastructure, or underwrite a named v2/red-team milestone. | A public pledge, grant memo, bounty, or signed term sheet. |
| **A host institution** | Announce a 90-day pilot: publish the rules, convene the panel, fund red-team bounties, and launch the first public scoreboard. | A public challenge page, panel roster, bounty pool, and live scoreboard. |
| **A journalist / media actor** | Publish or circulate one briefing focused on the scoreboard, the constitutional convention, and the upside/downside fork. | A story, memo, briefing, or internal note that the next participant can cite. |

The first sponsor milestones are: initiating host announced, rules published, expert panel formed, first bounty pool funded, first scoreboard live, first credible submissions received. The first public milestones after that are 1,024 verified participants, then 32,768, plus the first visibly serious pool. Once the mechanism clears those milestones, the question stops being "is this real?" and becomes "how fast is it compounding?"

## What To Do Right Now

1. **Deposit $1.** PRIZE deposit. It stays in the same pool until resolution. On failure, depositors divide the realized pool pro rata.
2. **Answer 2 questions.** 30 seconds. Treaty yes/no, allocation slider with evidence.
3. **Recruit 2 people.** Get two more verified participants onto the scoreboard.

### If You Have Reach, Do the Bigger Version Now

- **Funders:** pick one lane this week and publish the commitment so other participants can coordinate around it.
- **Researchers / builders:** publish one fork, attack, or replacement component this week rather than waiting for perfect certainty.
- **Host institutions:** announce a 90-day pilot, publish the rules, convene the panel, fund the first adversarial-review pool, and launch the scoreboard.
- **Media:** publish one briefing or story that treats the scoreboard and futures table as live public infrastructure, not a curiosity.

That is the ordinary-participant ask: three actions, under two minutes. If the prize fails, your deposit still has a pro-rata claim on the realized pool. If the prize succeeds, your PRIZE deposit helped push the world onto a far better branch. The mechanism is open, the scoreboard is public, and the first step is deliberately small. Whether it matters depends on how quickly enough people decide the arithmetic is worth acting on.

## FAQ for Skeptics

| Objection | Answer |
|:---|:---|
| "This will never work" | The ceiling cost of passage is {{< var treaty_campaign_total_cost >}} for the US, {{< var global_political_reform_investment >}} globally. ROI exceeds {{< var treaty_roi_existing_drugs_only >}} [@cost-of-change-paper-2025]. "Political impossibility" is a capital allocation problem, not a physics problem. |
| "Does this require trusting one institution?" | No. A credible host can initiate the network, but it should not be the root of trust. The rules, contracts, interfaces, and measurement layers should remain open, forkable, and replaceable so another host can continue the process if the first one fails. |
| "Does hosting mean endorsing v1?" | No. A host institution can endorse the convention, the metric standard, and the red-team process without declaring the current draft correct. Stage 1 exists to discover a better v2 if one exists. |
| "Someone will game the metrics" | Adversarial challenge bonds: anyone who catches gaming posts a bond, presents evidence, claws back the payout. |
| "I'd lose my $1" | On failure, depositors divide the realized pool pro rata. On success, the deposit funds the pool by design. The selfish case is that the rest of your life got much larger than the dollar you put in. |
| "Can I sell my claim?" | Not inside the protocol. PRIZE stays with the depositor's verified account until resolution. VOTE stays with the verified recruiter who earned it. Private contracts can exist outside the protocol, like assigning future royalties, but the protocol does not broker or enforce them. |
| "Why can't PRIZE be withdrawn early?" | Because a redeem-anytime exit right would let depositors drain the pool as success became more likely. The prize only works if the capital remains committed until the measurement date. |
| "What if I die or lose access?" | Claims belong to a verified account, not a fragile device. The system needs account recovery, beneficiary designation, and lawful successor control so a 15-year claim does not disappear because you lost your phone or your heirs need to prove who they are. |
| "Nobody else will participate" | That IS the problem the prize exists to solve. Your deposit is the proof that someone does. The scoreboard makes everyone else's participation visible. |
| "I don't understand the mechanism" | You do not need to. Deposit $1, answer 2 questions, recruit 2 people. |

## How It Starts

The instruments deploy in order, and each stage builds the audience for the next. A credible institution can be the initiating node for this process. That role is to host, convene, seed, and publish, not to become the sovereign of the mechanism. The rules, interfaces, and measurement layers should remain open and replaceable so launch does not create a single point of failure.

**Stage 1: The [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd) [@planetary-constitutional-convention-paper-2025] (weeks to months).** A credible host institution can initiate the network by publishing the rules, convening the expert panel, funding adversarial review, and launching the first public scoreboard. It does not need to endorse v1 as final truth. It hosts the convention that tries to replace it. Teams fork the [Earth Optimization Protocol v1](https://manual.warondisease.org), fix it or replace it. Expert panel filters for constitutional compliance. Adversarial review catches what the panel misses. [Wishocracy](../solution/wishocracy.qmd) [@wishocracy-paper-2025] ranks the survivors. The ratified version becomes v2. PRIZE deposits can begin during this stage, because the prize pool funds itself regardless of which plan is ratified.

**Stage 2: PRIZE deposits and the referendum (weeks to months).** PRIZE deposits are the simplest on-ramp. Every depositor learns what the prize is for. The PRIZE deposit is the simplest public coordination signal. Meanwhile, the [referendum platform](https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/global-referendum.html) launches: voters set their preferred military-to-health allocation via [wishocratic sliders](../solution/wishocracy.qmd), and every recruiter who brings a verified participant earns VOTE claims. The referendum grows because recruitment is rewarded.

**Stage 3: Scoreboard and momentum (months).** The referendum count climbs in public. The prize pool becomes large enough to be visibly real. Two dashboards matter: verified participant count and committed capital. Each new cohort of participants makes the next cohort easier to convince. Politicians notice.

**Stage 4: The lobbying campaign (months to years).** By now, millions of voters have registered preferences, the PRIZE pool is large enough to be taken seriously, and the scoreboard shows that the coalition is real. The [Earth Optimization Protocol](https://manual.warondisease.org/knowledge/strategy/earth-optimization-protocol-v1.html) [@earth-optimization-protocol-2025] describes how implementation financing converts the scoreboard into political pressure.

**Stage 5+: Implementation.** Once one binding path succeeds, budget authority starts shifting real resources. Implementers compete inside the winning Earth Optimization Protocol v2 to supply the cheapest verified pieces, and later challengers can still replace the whole plan if they genuinely dominate it.

The funnel is: the Planetary Constitutional Convention stress-tests the plan. PRIZE deposits create awareness. Awareness creates referendum voters. Voters earn VOTE claims. VOTE claims create an aligned recruiter base. The coalition provides the political pressure and financing base to pass the treaty. Each stage builds the coordination infrastructure for the next one. Nobody has to coordinate this centrally. The incentives coordinate it.

## The Starting Benchmark

The [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd) [@planetary-constitutional-convention-paper-2025] defines the process: ten required governance functions that any plan must cover (the Minimum Acceptable Governance table), eleven constitutional constraints no submission can violate, adversarial review from competing teams, and wishocratic pairwise comparison to rank the survivors. The [Earth Optimization Protocol v1](https://manual.warondisease.org) is the current benchmark. The convention exists to replace it.

## How the Prize Moves Money {#how-money-moves-full-mechanism}

Everything the prize exists to produce is either healthy life years or income. Paying separately for budget reallocation or trial enrollment is paying for plumbing that may or may not deliver water. Pay for water.

**The PRIZE pool trigger.** At year {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}}, if both targets are met (global HALE {{< var wishonia_projected_hale_year_15 >}}, global median income {{< var wishonia_trajectory_avg_income_year_15 >}}), the entire realized pool distributes to VOTE claimants. If not, depositors divide that same realized pool pro rata by deposits.

**Treasury release.** Separate from the binary PRIZE pool trigger, the implementation treasury releases funds proportionally as global terminal metrics improve, verified by peer-reviewed quasi-experimental study or RCT with causal attribution. The method: synthetic controls across staggered treaty adoption (countries sign at different times, providing a natural experiment), difference-in-differences with the Optimitron [@optimocracy-paper-2025] running continuous causal inference. The challenge-window mechanism provides adversarial review of attribution claims. The [1% Treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty.qmd) [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025] is adopted per-jurisdiction, and that staggered adoption is the causal identification strategy: signatories vs. non-signatories, handed to you for free.

**Why better ideas win, not extract.** If a superior proposal appears, VOTE claimants shift recruitment to it because doing so maximizes their own payout. The biggest reward is outcome perpetuity: a continuing share that only flows while results keep being produced. The protocol itself is replaceable: a strictly better selection mechanism replaces the current one under the same replacement rule. The two numbers do not change. Everything building toward them is improvable plumbing.

## Why Public Choice Theory Approves

Public choice theory says governments are run by humans who care about reelection, career advancement, and reputation. This is not a design flaw. It is a design constraint. The prize works with it, because no one has to become good:

- **Depositors** commit capital because they retain a failure-branch claim on the same pool and buy a better future on success.
- **Recruiters** recruit because every verified participant earns them a VOTE claim.
- **Entrepreneurs** compete for a giant implementation franchise.
- **Politicians** notice a growing scoreboard of verified voters who care about two numbers.
- **Researchers and auditors** compete for the authority to validate what works.
- **Citizens** get simpler choices and more visible returns from participation.

Every participant is doing exactly what they would do anyway, except pointed at diseases instead of each other.

## The Numbers

**How large can the prize pool get?** The canonical capital ceiling is the global retirement asset base: {{< var global_retirement_assets >}}. If that capital compounds through the wishocratic fund at {{< var prize_pool_annual_return >}} over {{< var prize_pool_resolution_years_nounit >}} years:

{{< var prize_pool_potential_max_size_latex >}}

The potential max pool is {{< var prize_pool_potential_max_size >}}. Reaching one year of the dysfunction tax ({{< var political_dysfunction_global_opportunity_cost_total >}}) by the resolution date requires {{< var prize_pool_target_required_principal >}} of starting capital, or {{< var prize_pool_target_pct_retirement_assets >}} of global retirement assets. That is {{< var prize_pool_target_pct_gdp >}} of global GDP and {{< var prize_pool_target_pct_wealth >}} of household wealth. The constraint is not money. It is the number of you who have done the arithmetic.

**How many people will actually vote?** The referendum is designed to solve the usual turnout problem:

| Dimension | Your elections | This referendum |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Effort** | Hours in line, research candidates | 30 seconds on a phone |
| **Financial reward** | $0 | {{< var vote_token_potential_value >}} modeled success payout |
| **Pivotality** | 1 in 30 million chance of changing outcome | Direct payout proportional to contribution |
| **Outcome fidelity** | Politician may ignore you after winning | Funds flow to verified implementation |

Your species turns out at 50-65% for elections despite getting paid nothing. This referendum adds a contingent payout, direct attribution, and a public scoreboard. The expected participation rate is {{< var vote_participation_rate >}}:

{{< var vote_expected_participants_latex >}}

At that rate, {{< var vote_expected_participants >}} people vote over the accumulation period, exceeding the Chenoweth passage threshold ({{< var treaty_campaign_voting_bloc_target >}}) by roughly 8x. Payout and participation are co-determined: the potential max pool is fixed, so more voters means a smaller per-claim payout. But dilution does not erase the incentive. At the CI lower bound (3% participation), the modeled success payout is about $123K per claim. At the CI upper bound (70%), it is still about $5.3K per claim. That range is enough to make recruitment a serious activity rather than volunteer theater. The potential payout per VOTE claim at {{< var vote_participation_rate >}} participation:

{{< var vote_token_potential_value_latex >}}

**Why more pools make everyone richer.** The protocol does not need a single pool. It needs a single *metric standard*. Any pool that measures the same two terminal outcomes (median HALY, median income) and uses proof-of-personhood for deduplication automatically joins the reward network. A verified person claims proportionally from every participating pool, regardless of which one recorded their vote. Japan launches a pool, the EU launches a pool, the Gates Foundation launches a pool. The combined reward grows with each new entrant. A "competing" pool is actually a deposit. Spending money to "attack" the network is indistinguishable from donating to it. Think of email: you can run your own server; all servers interoperate; running your own extends the network rather than fragmenting it.

**What the protocol must solve.** Six capabilities: (1) identity layer (one person, one vote, cross-pool), (2) pool registry, (3) cross-pool claim settlement, (4) scoreboard aggregation, (5) terminal metric oracle, (6) claim mechanics. The companion [protocol specification](../appendix/earth-optimization-prize-protocol.qmd) [@earth-optimization-protocol-2025] specifies how.

## What v1 Claims (and What You Need to Beat)

The full table of what the [Earth Optimization Protocol v1](https://manual.warondisease.org) claims, paper by paper, and the specific benchmarks a competing plan must beat, is in the [Planetary Constitutional Convention](planetary-constitutional-convention.qmd) [@planetary-constitutional-convention-paper-2025]. The prize asks one question: *who can cause verified implementation of a complete package that wins on welfare per dollar?* We wrote v1 because competitions need a starting entry. We expect to lose.

## Why This Works or Gets Replaced

There are only two stable outcomes:

1. **The [Earth Optimization Protocol v1](https://manual.warondisease.org) is mostly right but incomplete.** Then whoever augments it with the missing functions and causes implementation receives the prize. The result is the Earth Optimization Protocol v2.
2. **A strict improvement exists.** Then whoever builds and implements that improvement receives the prize instead (also the Earth Optimization Protocol v2), provided it dominates the Minimum Acceptable Governance function by function rather than skipping inconvenient pieces.

Those are the only serious possibilities. The unserious possibility is the one humans choose by default: endless argument with no implementation market. Either way, the prize produces the Earth Optimization Protocol v2 and causes its implementation. People are dying at {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily_nounit >}} per day while your species argues about mechanism design. Please improve or replace v1 as quickly as possible.

> Reward whoever causes the most people to stop dying and start earning more, using any legal method, or replace the current best attempt with a better one.

One institution may initiate the network. No institution should be able to stop it.

The mechanism does not need participants to be wise. It needs them to be self-interested, impatient, and capable of reading a scoreboard. The remaining variable is how long this takes to become obvious enough to act on.
